sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is by the claimant for enhancement of compensation awarded in MVC No.194/2015 by the I-Addl.
Senior Civil Judge & MACT-Kalaburagi (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for short) dated 14.08.2017.
2. With consent of both the side, the matter is taken up for final disposal, though it is slated for admission.
The parties will be referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for sake of convenience.
4. Brief facts of the case are that on 24.06.2014 claimant along with deceased-Raju who was rider of the motorcycle, were going on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 32/ED-3654 towards Kodambal.
At Mustari village, they met with an accident due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-39/J-1376 by its rider.
As a result of which the said Raju as well as the petitioner sustained severe injuries.
Petitioner was admitted to Hospital for treatment, she had sustained grievous injuries.
Due to the said accident, she has been suffering from permanent disability, which is affecting her earning capacity.
With these reasons she prayed to award the compensation.
5. The respondent-insurance company denied the contents of the claim petition and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

Smt.Mallamma vs Ishwar And Ors on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126064987/
2 NC: 2024:KHC-K:4933 6.
Tribunal had framed the necessary issues.
7. In MVC No.194/2015 and MVC No.195/2015 were clubbed together by the Tribunal and common evidence was recorded.
Claimants examined PWs.1 to 3 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 16.

The respondent No.2 examined RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.
8.

The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence available on record,
assessed age of claimant as 45 years, notional income Rs.6,000/- per month, added 30% future prospects, disability at 6%, multiplier '14' and on that basis had awarded the following amount of compensation.

Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Pain and suffering Rs.25,000-00
2 . Medical Expenses Rs.10,000-00  3. Attendant and Conveyance Rs.500-00  charges  4. Loss of future income Rs.78,624-00  Total Rs.1,14,124-00  NC: 2024:KHC-K:4933 9.
The Tribunal also held that due to composite negligence of riders of both the motorcycle, accident had taken place.
Therefore, respondent No.1 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount and respondent Nos.2 and 3 shall pay remaining 50%.
The same is challenged in the present appeal on the ground of quantum of compensation as well as apportionment of liability to pay the compensation.
10. Heard the arguments of learned counsels for both side.

11. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 produced judgment passed by the Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.201058/2018 dated 10.07.2020, wherein the claimants in MVC No.195/2015 have challenged the quantum of compensation as well as apportionment of negligence.
The Division Bench after hearing both the parties, upheld the finding of the Tribunal regarding contributory negligence however enhanced the amount of compensation.
In view of the findings of the Division NC: 2024:KHC-K:4933 Bench, the said point of composite negligence of both riders of vehicle is adjudicated and this Court need not reconsider the same.
12. The income of the claimant taken by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
As per chart of income prepared by the KSLSA, income of claimant could be taken as Rs.7,500/-per month.

Smt.Mallamma vs Ishwar And Ors on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126064987/
3 13.
The Tribunal has not considered loss of income during laid up period and amount of compensation awarded towards medical expenses and incidental expenses also on lower side.
14. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of injuries, it is proper to enhance global compensation of Rs.25,000/- on all the heads.

Accordingly, I pass the following;
 ORDER  i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

The impugned judgment and award passed by the I-Addl. Senior Civil Judge & MACT-Kalaburagi in MVC.No.194/2015 dated 14.08.2017, is modified;
 a) The claimant is entitled for global  compensation of Rs.25,000/- in addition to whatever amount awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The respondent - insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order to the extent of its liability.
iv. The amount enhanced is not much therefore, entire amount is ordered to be released in favour of the claimant after due identification (in MVC No.194/2015).

The registry is directed to send Trial Court  Records along with a copy of this Smt.Mallamma vs Ishwar And Ors on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126064987/
